On Wed, Nov 7, 2012 at 4:21 AM, Steffen <steffe...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear unmarked users/developers,

We are trying to estimate population trends for a passerine bird species surveyed on 50 transects every year. In each year, each transect is surveyed 3 times and birds are recorded in 3 distance categories, so we have R=50, T=3 and J=3 for every year, and I am wondering whether there is an option to extent the gdistsamp model to a multi-year case to estimate population change between years?

So far I have simply stacked the data on top of each other (e.g. R=100 'year-sites' for n=2 years) , and included 'Year' as a site covariate in models:

null <- gdistsamp(~ Year, ~ 1, ~1, data= AQWAdis, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="ha", mixture = "P", K=200)

This provides a population-level density estimate for each year, but ignores the serial correlation within transects among years. I am wondering whether that information could somehow be incorporated in gdistsamp (somewhat analogous to this paper: Kéry et al. (2009) Trend estimation in populations with imperfect detection. Journal of Applied Ecology, 46, 1163-1172.)?

Any information would be greatly appreciated!

cheers,

steffen
